Welcome to The Woodlands School
Welcome to our school website, I hope you are able to find all the information that you require.
The Woodlands School is a specialist provision for children and young people with Autism or Social Communication Difficulties Disorder with associated learning difficulties. We are a proud, vibrant community dedicated to the education and development of students with Autism. We firmly believe that disability does not limit what individuals can achieve. Our commitment is to foster an environment where each student is valued for their unique strengths and abilities.
At The Woodlands School, we celebrate the achievements of our students, both big and small. Every milestone reached is a testament to their hard work and resilience. We understand that every child learns at their own pace, and it is our mission to provide personalised support that encourages growth and independence. My experienced staff employ a variety of teaching methods and approaches tailored to meet the diverse needs of our students, ensuring that each one has the opportunity to thrive.
We recognise that education is about more than academic success; it is also about preparing students for life beyond school. With this in mind, we focus on developing essential life skills that empower our students to become independent, successful adults. We engage in collaborative partnerships with families, professionals and the local community to create an inclusive atmosphere that nurtures personal development.
We are deeply passionate about supporting students on their educational journeys. We strive to create an inclusive and accepting environment where diversity is embraced, and every individual’s potential is realised. Together, we cultivate a climate of positivity, respect, and mutual support, helping each student to reach their full potential.
We have three Campuses in Milton Keynes. Our Primary Department is sited at Hertford Place in Bletchley. The Middle and Upper Departments are at Hazeley and a further secondary campus at Galley Hill.
For prospective parents and professionals 'Our offer' page articulates for you our provision.

Parents/Carers
Parents & Carers
At The Woodlands School we understand the importance of working collaboratively with our pupils, and parents and carers to ensure that together we achieve the best possible outcomes for our students.
We know that effective partnership requires active parental engagement. Staff work hard to provide families with individualised support, whilst offering an extensive parent training programme.
"We know that it is only together that we can make the difference."

About Us
Admissions/Entry criteria
The local authority is the admissions officer for The Woodlands School therefore, all referrals and appeals are managed by the Special Educational Needs Department. www.milton-keynes.gov.uk
All children admitted to the school must possess an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), which outlines their specific needs and challenges. We welcome applications from children and young people at any stage of their educational journey, recognising that each path is unique.
As a special school tailored for individuals with Autism and associated learning difficulties, our curriculum is meticulously crafted to address the primary needs of those on the Autism Spectrum. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and nurturing environment where students can flourish academically and socially.
It is important to note that The Woodlands School is not equipped to accommodate students whose primary needs stem from Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) difficulties or where severe learning difficulties is the primary need, even though there is also a diagnosis of Autism. Furthermore, we do not offer GCSE qualifications nor do we provide a fully sensory-based curriculum, as our focus remains squarely on meeting the diverse needs of our students within the parameters of Autism.
The Leadership Team are always delighted to show parents around where the child lives within Milton Keynes City, has an Education, Health and Care Plan and has been identified as requiring a specialist provision. Due to the challenges of our students, and the need for consistency and routine, we must put their well-being at the forefront and limit disruptions.
However, parents should note that an invitation to visit does not constitute an offer of a place, nor does it indicate that the final outcome of an assessment will be a recommendation that your child comes to a school like The Woodlands School; such decisions remain the responsibility of the Milton Keynes Council's Special Educational Needs (SEN) Team. Please click on MKC SEND to obtain further information.

Our Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) programme is designed to empower our young people to develop the skills, confidence and independence they need for adult life, whether this leads to employment, further education, supported internships, volunteering, or community participation.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Woodlands School - Reading at home
pageCache.text:
Home Learning
Reading at home
At the Woodlands School we follow a systematic approach to teaching reading called Essential Letters and Sounds. We teach the pupils to read through the act of decoding and blending. Essential Letters and Sounds teaches children the link between the sounds of our language (phonemes) and the written representation of these sounds (graphemes), or the spellings of the sounds contained within the English language. Teaching of phonics is tailored to the individual child who will move through the programme at the pace necessary for them to be successful.
It must always be remembered that phonics is the step up to word recognition. Automatic reading of all words – decodable and tricky – is the ultimate goal. Once our pupils have completed the Essential letters and Sounds programme they become free readers where reading for fluency and comprehension are the focus
Reading for pleasure
At the Woodlands school we value the importance of promoting a love of reading. Reading for pleasure opens up new worlds for children. It gives them the opportunity to use their imagination to explore new ideas, visit new places and meet new characters. Interestingly, reading for pleasure also improves children’s well-being and empathy. It helps them to understand their own identity, and gives them an insight into the world and the views of others. Our school environment including our libraries and allocated book areas of the classrooms include a range of texts to spark interest and imagination.
How can you help at home?
If your child is working on the Essential letters and sounds phonics programme their class teacher will set reading books at an appropriate level for their decoding skills. These can be accessed through the website
https://www.oxfordowl.co.uk/ under the ‘student’ tab. Any opportunities to practise reading skills will help so setting aside some time for your child to read their set book with you will be hugely beneficial.
You can also encourage reading for pleasure at home and here are some top tips to help you do this:
Value the books they read- all reading is valuable for a child’s development. Some of us prefer non-fiction; some of us prefer comics. One child might like superhero books; another might a book of football statistics
Set aside some special reading time- just a few minutes a day is enough to create a reading habit
Get caught reading yourself – show that reading for pleasure is not just for children
Stage and screen – use your child’s favourite films or games as a springboard into reading. Knowing the characters and storyline can be a helpful bridge into reading a longer story.
Read to each other – if your child really doesn’t want to read on their own, then read together. You read a page, then they read a page. Or one of you could read any dialogue. Be brave and put on different voices.

Our Offer
The Curriculum
The school has developed a curriculum adapting the National Curriculum for our students and this is used to produce our own Progression Documents and Teaching Plans. Students in our Upper Department follow a curriculum developed from the National Curriculum which follows a qualification and vocational pathway.
All pupils at The Woodlands School have Education, Health and Care Plans. These are used to ensure the pupils are kept at the centre of their learning.
To ensure we meet the learning needs of all our students our curriculum is designed into learning pathways. The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) has a one year programme for pupils in Reception. The curriculum from Year 1 to Year 9 has been constructed with pathways to ensure that the curriculum is relevant to students and the level at which they are working at. The pathways are:
Discovery Pathway: The Discovery Pathway is a primary-only provision, designed for pupils who benefit from a play-based, sensory, experiential and structured approach to learning. Rooted in the EYFS Statutory Framework and taking account of relevant National Curriculum objectives, the pathway provides engaging and meaningful learning experiences tailored to each pupil’s individual needs.
Thrive Pathway: The Thrive pathway is designed for students who are in need of a more sensory-based approach to learning with an emphasis on engagement and early development. Students follow basic routines and structure to enable them to learn as effectively as possible.
Aspire Pathway: The Aspire pathway is followed by the majority of students at the Woodlands School. The pupils usually follow a highly structured approach to learning to start with and then progresses to a more traditional approach to learning.
From Years 10 to 14 the students follow a similar curriculum but with a more vocational based approach. This is also split into two pathways:
Personal: This pathway is very similar to the Thrive pathway above but will give the young person increased opportunities to experience the local community and prepare them for life after school.
Vocational: This pathway follows on from the Aspire pathway and is designed to support the young person's learning whilst giving them the chance to prepare for employment or further education after school.
Please use the contents to the right of the page to go each subject for more information. For further information please contact me via the school office on 01908 563885 or admin@twsmk.co.uk
Right to Withdraw from Religious Education (RE)At The Woodlands School, we recognise that parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE) if they wish. We encourage families to discuss any concerns or questions about the RE curriculum with the school before making a decision, so that we can provide information and support. If you decide to withdraw your child, please contact the Headteacher in writing to make suitable arrangements.
